title: Props Basics
description: Learn how to pass data to components using props.

data.text: **Props** (short for properties) let you pass data from a parent component to a child component. Props are read-only and make components reusable — the same component can display different data depending on the props it receives.
Props look like HTML attributes. You can pass strings, numbers, booleans, objects, arrays, and functions.

data.title: Passing Different Types
data.content: Strings, numbers, booleans, objects, and functions as props

data.text: Inside a functional component, props arrive as a single object. You can access properties with dot notation or destructure them directly in the parameter list.

data.title: Accessing Props
Destructure for Readability
data.text: Destructuring props in the function signature keeps JSX clean and makes it obvious which props the component expects.
Never modify props inside a child component. Props are owned by the parent. If a child needs to change a value, the parent should pass an updater function as a prop instead.

data.title: Do Not Mutate Props

data.text: React follows a strict **one-way data flow**: data moves down from parent to child via props. This makes the app predictable — you can trace where any value came from by following the props.

data.caption: Data flows down from parent to child via props.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Parent State] -->|props| B[Child A]
    A -->|props| C[Child B]
    B -->|no reverse flow| A

terms.definition: Read-only inputs passed from parent to child components.

data.title: Exercise: Pass Props Through Three Levels
data.description: Practice passing props through multiple component layers.
steps: Create a GrandParent component with a 'title' state.
Create a Parent component that receives title and a subtitle as props.
Create a Child component that receives both and renders them in an h1 and h2.
Render GrandParent in App.jsx and verify the data flows correctly.
data.expectedOutcome: Data passes from grandparent to child without breaking the one-way flow rule.

items.question: Can I change props inside a child?
items.answer: No. Props are read-only. If a child needs to modify a value, the parent should lift the state up and pass a setter function as a prop.

items.question: What happens if I pass a prop that the child does not use?
items.answer: React ignores extra props. They do not cause errors, but they increase memory usage slightly.

items.question: Can props be any JavaScript type?
items.answer: Yes. Props can be strings, numbers, booleans, objects, arrays, functions, and even other React elements.

items.question: Are props shared across all instances of a component?
items.answer: No. Each instance receives its own props object from its parent. Changes to one instance's props do not affect others.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Props pass data from parent to child components.
Props are read-only — children cannot modify them.
Use destructuring for cleaner component signatures.
React enforces one-way data flow for predictability.
data.takeaway: Props are the foundation of component communication. Next, you will explore advanced prop patterns.
